_comment: memory_inject_max_bytes caps what the remember plugin's SessionStart hook cat's into every session; a file over the cap is NAMED rather than injected, and stays greppable on disk. The rule this cap encodes: inject the live buffer, name the history, and let the reader grep what is named -- which is what the SessionStart banner already says to do with the rotated archives. Top-level _-prefixed keys are stripped at merge time by lib-memory-dir.sh, so this comment never reaches config(). RAISED 1400 -> 2500 on 2026-08-29. The 1400 was measured on 2026-08-21 against a now.md of 913 bytes, and now.md is a buffer that GROWS through the day until consolidation flushes it -- so the cap started dropping the one file it exists to keep, silently, partway through most days. now.md was observed at 2356 bytes mid-session on 2026-08-29. 2500 covers that. The cap CANNOT do both of its jobs at once, and this is the trade that was taken rather than a headroom figure: one threshold applies to every file, so any value large enough to hold a grown now.md also admits recent.md (2147 bytes on 2026-08-29, the next file up). At 2500 the store injects now.md and recent.md and names archive.md (3491) and the daily files (~9 KB each), so roughly 4.6 KB where the pre-cap store injected ~10.4 KB. Re-measure recent.md before changing this number; it is what sets the ceiling. This is a stopgap, and the durable fix is not ours to make: the injector is the upstream claude-plugins-official/remember hook (scripts/session-start-hook.sh) and it DROPS an over-cap file rather than truncating it, so a buffer past any threshold vanishes whole instead of degrading. Truncation upstream would end the trade.
